pid_data.process_description: 100T-01 serves as a buffer between the existing process unit battery-limit naphtha source and the Hydrogen Production Unit (HPU), with a design capacity sized for five days of inventory at the HPU rated naphtha flow rate. Liquid naphtha is received from B/L into the naphtha storage tank through the inlet transfer piping and shutdown isolation arrangement, stored in 100T-01, and then routed from the tank outlet to the naphtha transfer pumps 100P-01A/B for continuous supply to the HPU. The tank is shown as a naphtha storage tank with an internal floating roof/IFR service intent, manholes, level instrumentation, pressure indication, temperature indication, nitrogen blanketing, atmospheric venting, emergency venting, and drain connections to OWS/CSS. The tank operates at 38 degC and 0.01 barg, with design limits of 43/-8 degC and 0.07/-0.06 barg. Nitrogen blanketing is provided through the NG line and PCV-0101 for in-breathing to mitigate vapor losses and prevent formation of flammable vapor/air mixtures. Tank out-breathing is controlled by PCV-0102 through a vent line routed via an activated carbon canister to ATM at a safe location. Secondary overpressure/vacuum and emergency protection are provided by PVV-0102 and EH-0101, and PSV-0101 provides thermal relief for trapped liquid in the transfer piping. Safety interlocks manage liquid inventory: LSHH-0102 associated with IS-09 trips/closes the inlet shutdown valve UV-0102 to prevent overfilling, while LSLL-0102 associated with IS-10 stops the naphtha transfer pumps 100P-01A/B and closes the outlet shutdown valve UV-0102 to prevent pump dry running. Naphtha is transferred to the HPU at a nominal flow rate of 37 m3/h, equivalent to 24,496 kg/h at density 660 kg/m3. Pump protection is provided by a continuous minimum-flow return of 8.6 m3/h, equivalent to 5,653 kg/h, through RO-0101 back to 100T-01. Discharge flow monitoring is provided by FT-0101/FI-0101 with FY-0101, and pump discharge pressure is locally indicated by PG-0101A and PG-0101B. Emergency interlock IS-28 is initiated by HS-0101A/HS-0101B and executes total system isolation by closing the naphtha inlet and outlet UV-0102 shutdown valves and tripping the naphtha transfer pumps 100P-01A/B.
pid_data.intention: The intended operation is to receive liquid naphtha from the existing process unit, maintain a stable five-day storage inventory in 100T-01, and continuously deliver naphtha to the HPU through 100P-01A/B at a constant rated flow of 37 m3/h, equivalent to 24,496 kg/h at density 660 kg/m3. The tank system is designed to preserve product availability during upstream process unit shutdown or outage, while maintaining safe storage at 0.01 barg and 38 degC within design limits of 0.07/-0.06 barg and 43/-8 degC. Nitrogen blanketing via PCV-0101 is intended to prevent air ingress and flammable mixture formation during in-breathing, while PCV-0102 routes out-breathing vapors through activated carbon to ATM at a safe location to limit vapor emissions. Inventory stability and pump protection are maintained by level indication/alarms and interlocks: high-high level initiates IS-09 to close the inlet UV-0102 and prevent tank overfill, low-low level initiates IS-10 to shut down 100P-01A/B and close the outlet UV-0102 to avoid dry running, and manual emergency action through HS-0101A/HS-0101B initiates IS-28 to isolate inlet/outlet and trip the pumps. A continuous minimum-flow recycle of 8.6 m3/h through RO-0101 is intended to keep the operating pump within its safe hydraulic envelope, while flow and temperature indication on the HPU transfer line support stable feed quality and reliable HPU operation.

equipment.name: Naphtha Transfer Pump A

connections.node: Naphtha Tank Storage (100T-01) with Naphtha Transfer Pump (100P-01A/B) including inlet transfer line from the Process Unit, and outlet transfer line from the Naphtha Tank (100T-01) back to the HPU via the Naphtha Transfer Pump (100P-01 A/B)
connections.node_boundary: The node starts at the existing process unit naphtha B/L inlet and NG/IA utility boundaries, includes the inlet shutdown and tank receipt piping, 100T-01 with blanketing, venting, relief, level/temperature/pressure instrumentation and drains, the tank outlet/suction piping to 100P-01A/B, pump discharge headers, minimum-flow recycle to tank, and ends at the HPU B/L naphtha outlet plus ATM/OWS/CSS discharge boundaries.
connections.flow_direction: Naphtha flows from the existing process unit/B/L into 100T-01, then from 100T-01 through the outlet line to the suction of 100P-01A or 100P-01B. The operating pump discharges to the common discharge header and onward to the HPU B/L, with a continuous minimum-flow recycle returning from the pump discharge header through RO-0101 back to 100T-01. Nitrogen flows from the NG header into the tank vapor space through PCV-0101, while tank vapors flow out through PCV-0102 and AC-0101 to ATM at a safe location during out-breathing. Drain flows leave the tank/bund area to OWS/CSS as shown.
connections.context: Single user-defined HAZOP node. Main deviation coverage includes no/low naphtha feed to HPU, high/low tank level, tank overfill, pump dry running, blocked outlet, pump deadhead, low minimum-flow recycle, high/low tank pressure, nitrogen blanketing failure, air ingress, excessive venting/vapor emission, thermal expansion of blocked-in liquid requiring PSV-0101, reverse flow through pump or inlet line, spurious or failed shutdown of UV-0102, and loss of IA affecting actuated valves. Preserved metadata: tank OP 0.01 barg, DP 0.07/-0.06 barg, OT 38 degC, DT 43/-8 degC; HPU transfer flow 37 m3/h or 24,496 kg/h at density 660 kg/m3; minimum recycle 8.6 m3/h or 5,653 kg/h via RO-0101; UV-0102 marked FC-TSO; PSV-0101 associated locked-open block valves marked LO/LO; line labels include 100-P-021-A2-1F-4 inch, 100-P-022-A2-1F-6 inch, 100-P-024-A2-1F-6 inch, 100-P-025/026/027-A2-1F-4 inch, 100-P-029-A2-1F-2 inch, 100-NG lines, OWS/SW/CSS lines.
